assessments.disposition: accepted for the approved disposable wrapper
assessments.evidence: Wrapper initdb creates a unique mktemp cluster under /tmp, trust-authenticated fixture superuser jadpo_auth_test, loopback-only PostgreSQL and a freshly allocated port. Persistence and prior auth fixtures have separate databases; a third dedicated jadpo_readiness_recovery_runtime holds the connection-loss fixture. Control connects to postgres in this same cluster, not the deliberately disabled application database. Four explicit postgres:// URLs use this exact host/port/user and fixed paths. Both wrapper and verifier remove inherited readiness URL bindings before dispatch.
assessments.limit: URL matching is an endpoint guard, not standalone proof of disposable ownership. Directly supplying a matching local pair outside this wrapper is not the approved execution path; production or existing application databases are not authorized targets.

assessments.evidence: Before SQL control allocation or fault injection, application protocol must be postgres:, hostname 127.0.0.1, nonempty port, username jadpo_auth_test and exact /jadpo_readiness_recovery_runtime path. Control protocol/hostname/port/username match the application and its exact path is /postgres. Independent execution of this exact source guard accepts the intended pair and rejects 11 invalid/mismatched pairs, including two opaque-origin URLs differing only by port.
assessments.limit: No reliance on URL.origin; both tested PostgreSQL origins are null. Guard probes execute assertions only, without SQL/network.

assessments.evidence: One fixed ALTER DATABASE jadpo_readiness_recovery_runtime ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false prevents pool reconnection. The subsequent pg_terminate_backend query uses a bound exact datname and excludes its own backend; results must be nonempty and all true. The control database remains available to restore ALLOW_CONNECTIONS. This is actual dropped app/auth-storage connections plus rejected new connections, not a mocked outage or table-only rename. No dynamic database identifier or request data is interpolated into the ALTER statement.
assessments.limit: No server stop/restart or termination of backends for other database names; scope is the one database inside the disposable cluster.

assessments.evidence: After healthy startup and a successful authenticated request, the test injects the fault and polls until generated /health/ready actually returns 503. Any pre-expiry cached successes must be 200; failure body is checked exactly before the 32-request outage burst, which must all be 503/not_ready/database unavailable/empty advisories. On restoring connections, repeated 32-request bursts may contain safe matching 200/503 bodies until one full burst of 32 ready responses is observed.
assessments.limit: This observes the failure transition beyond the healthy cache; it does not assume a fixed sleep crosses the cache. Generated code retains a 1000ms healthy cache and retry backoff. 8-second fetch/poll budgets and outer 30-second test timeout are test controls, not product deadline guarantees. No PG schema initialization-count or precise simultaneous-start/in-flight instrumentation.

assessments.area: Same process, credential and authority state
assessments.evidence: The test spawns one generated-app host child, provisions/issues once before outage, then reuses the identical headers object and issued credential during outage and after recovery. Protected identity is gated with safe dependency_unavailable/503 while storage is unavailable. /health/live remains exactly live/200. After recovery identity returns the same fixed user ID/200, and child.exitCode stays null. No second issuance, restart or respawn occurs in the test.
assessments.limit: The localhost test-only host issues a fixture credential through the generated authentication host; this does not authorize public provisioning endpoints or arbitrary user/service authority.

assessments.evidence: The exact outage/readiness bodies and safe identity error are checked for absence of both signing-key canaries, the credential, application/control database URLs, recovery database name, 57P01, 55000 and raw SELECT. Every checked recovery-burst body is also screened. Both complete stdout/stderr streams are collected after the sole child exits and screened by the same assertSafe function. Independent execution passed these assertions; recovered identity body is exact.
assessments.limit: No general logging/redaction proof, all possible native errors, debug-stack-enabled mode or exhaustive response vocabulary qualification.

assessments.disposition: accepted for normal and assertion-failure structured control flow
assessments.evidence: connectionsDisabled tracks successful disabling; the outer finally re-enables if needed. Nested finally kills/awaits the sole child and closes the control pool even when restore fails. The wrapper traps EXIT, INT and TERM, stops only its newly created cluster by exact -D path, and removes its unique mktemp root. Suite afterAll removes only its own unique temporary output/database root. The independent wrapper returned exit 0 through this normal cleanup path.
assessments.limit: No injected cleanup-failure test or SIGKILL/host-crash guarantee. Existing shell cleanup tolerates pg_ctl stop failures. A process-list diagnostic was sandbox-denied, so no independent process/filesystem forensic teardown audit is claimed.

assessments.evidence: Independent AST execution of the exact environment=os.environ.copy() assignment and following pop loop from tools/verify.py removes all four supplied readiness URL canaries while preserving an unrelated canary. No full verifier execution occurs in that probe. Only postgres.sh readiness intentionally sets test/auth/recovery/control URLs for the selected suite; normal non-PG readiness run cannot inherit these URLs through the verifier.
assessments.limit: This is the requested four-key isolation review, not review of every unrelated verifier environment variable or mode.

import ast, json, types
from pathlib import Path
source=Path('tools/verify.py').read_text()
module=ast.parse(source)
main=next(n for n in module.body if isinstance(n,ast.FunctionDef) and n.name=='main')
start=next(i for i,n in enumerate(main.body) if isinstance(n,ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(t,ast.Name) and t.id=='environment' for t in n.targets))
nodes=main.body[start:start+2]
keys=['JADPO_READINESS_TEST_DATABASE_URL','JADPO_READINESS_AUTH_DATABASE_URL','JADPO_READINESS_RECOVERY_DATABASE_URL','JADPO_READINESS_CONTROL_DATABASE_URL']
canaries={k:'unused-inherited-canary' for k in keys}
canaries['SAFE_UNRELATED_TEST_MARKER']='preserved'
context={'os':types.SimpleNamespace(environ=canaries)}
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=nodes,type_ignores=[]),'tools/verify.py:exact-environment-isolation','exec'),context)
environment=context['environment']
assert all(k not in environment for k in keys)
assert environment['SAFE_UNRELATED_TEST_MARKER']=='preserved'
print(json.dumps({'executedExactAstStatements':len(nodes),'removed':keys,'unrelatedPreserved':True,'fullGateExecuted':False}))
